import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML

# Helper to assert that the function returns the same result as the old implementation
# for the given inputs. Since we only have the new implementation, we encode the
# expected behaviour based on the original regex semantics.

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str,expected",
    [
        # Basic known entities
        ("&", "&"),
        ("<div>", "<div>"),
        ("Hello "World"!", 'Hello "World"!'),

        # Multiple known entities
        ("a < b & c > d", "a < b & c > d"),

        # Unknown entity should remain unchanged
        ("&unknown;", "&unknown;"),

        # Entity containing an internal '&' should NOT be transformed (old regex would not match)
        ("&foo&bar;", "&foo&bar;"),

        # Mixed known and unknown/internal‑ampersand entities
        ("Start & middle &foo&bar; end", "Start & middle &foo&bar; end"),

        # Leading and trailing ampersands that are not part of an entity
        ("&&&&", "&&&&"),
    ],
)
def test_unescapeHTML_behaviour(input_str, expected):
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected


def test_unescapeHTML_none():
    assert unescapeHTML(None) is None


def test_unescapeHTML_type_assertion():
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        unescapeHTML(123)          # not a compat_str (i.e., not a str)
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        unescapeHTML(b"bytes")     # bytes also should raise
